### Problem: Valid palindrome after one deletion {#sec-test-p1-palindrome}

::: {.p-statement}
Given a string $s$ of lowercase letters ($1 \le |s| \le 10^5$), return `true` if $s$ can become a palindrome after deleting **at most one** character.

Source: [LC 680 · Valid Palindrome II](https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-palindrome-ii/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Compare from both ends. While the characters match, the deletion is not needed there. At the first mismatch $s_i \ne s_j$, one of the two must be deleted, but you cannot tell which by looking at neighbours: try **both**, and check whether $s[i+1..j]$ or $s[i..j-1]$ is a palindrome.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Brute force.** Try the string itself and every string with one character deleted: $O(n^2)$.
2. **Bug 1: skip only one side.** At the mismatch, try only $s[i+1..j]$. Wrong on `"bba"`: deleting the `a` on the right works, deleting the `b` on the left does not.
3. **Bug 2: guess the side from the next character.** "If $s_{i+1} = s_j$ skip the left character, else skip the right one." When **both** neighbours match, the guess can pick the wrong side and never recover. This is the bug that passes many hand-made tests.
4. **Refined.** At the first mismatch, return `is_pal(i + 1, j) or is_pal(i, j - 1)`. **Invariant:** before the mismatch, $s[0..i)$ and $s(j..n)$ mirror each other, so any valid deletion must remove $s_i$ or $s_j$ (or a character that can be swapped for one of them in the matched part, which gives the same string).

**How testing finds the bugs.** Both bugs need repeated letters around the mismatch. Over the alphabet `"ab"` the stress test finds them in a few tests; over 26 letters, random strings are almost never one deletion away from a palindrome, so both versions just answer `false` and agree with the brute force.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
#### Python

```{python}
#| label: test-palindrome
def is_pal(s, i, j):
    while i < j:
        if s[i] != s[j]:
            return False
        i, j = i + 1, j - 1
    return True

def valid_palindrome(s):
    i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
    while i < j:
        if s[i] != s[j]:
            return is_pal(s, i + 1, j) or is_pal(s, i, j - 1)
        i, j = i + 1, j - 1
    return True

def valid_skip_left(s):                              # bug 1: tries only one side
    i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
    while i < j:
        if s[i] != s[j]:
            return is_pal(s, i + 1, j)
        i, j = i + 1, j - 1
    return True

def valid_guess_side(s):                             # bug 2: guesses the side from a neighbour
    i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
    while i < j:
        if s[i] != s[j]:
            if s[i + 1] == s[j]:
                return is_pal(s, i + 1, j)
            return is_pal(s, i, j - 1)
        i, j = i + 1, j - 1
    return True

def valid_brute(s):
    return any(t == t[::-1] for t in [s] + [s[:k] + s[k + 1:] for k in range(len(s))])

gen_ab = lambda: (rand_string(random.randint(1, 10), "ab"),)
gen_az = lambda: (rand_string(random.randint(1, 10), "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"),)

assert stress(gen_az, valid_guess_side, valid_brute, trials=500) is None   # natural tests miss it
bug1 = stress(gen_ab, valid_skip_left, valid_brute)
bug2 = stress(gen_ab, valid_guess_side, valid_brute)
small1 = shrink(bug1[0], lambda c: valid_skip_left(*c) != valid_brute(*c),
                lambda c: ((t,) for t in (c[0][:k] + c[0][k + 1:] for k in range(len(c[0])))))
small2 = shrink(bug2[0], lambda c: valid_guess_side(*c) != valid_brute(*c),
                lambda c: ((t,) for t in (c[0][:k] + c[0][k + 1:] for k in range(len(c[0])))))
print("skip-left bug fails on", bug1[0], "-> shrunk to", small1[0])
print("guess-side bug fails on", bug2[0], "-> shrunk to", small2[0])
assert len(small1[0]) == 3
assert stress(gen_ab, valid_palindrome, valid_brute, trials=3000) is None
assert all(valid_palindrome(s) == valid_brute(s) for s in ("".join(p) for n in range(1, 9) for p in product("abc", repeat=n)))

assert valid_palindrome("aba") and valid_palindrome("abca") and not valid_palindrome("abc")
assert valid_palindrome("bba") and not valid_skip_left("bba")
```

#### C++

```cpp
bool isPal(const string& s, int i, int j) {
    while (i < j) if (s[i++] != s[j--]) return false;
    return true;
}

bool validPalindrome(const string& s) {
    int i = 0, j = (int)s.size() - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (s[i] != s[j]) return isPal(s, i + 1, j) || isPal(s, i, j - 1);
        ++i; --j;
    }
    return true;
}
```
:::

::: {#fig-test-p1-palindrome}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
s = small2[0]
i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
while s[i] == s[j]:
    i, j = i + 1, j - 1
left_ok, right_ok = is_pal(s, i + 1, j), is_pal(s, i, j - 1)
assert not left_ok and right_ok and s[i + 1] == s[j]

def draw(ax, p):
    V.array(ax, p, list(s), 0, 0, pointers=[(i, "i", "indigo", "top"), (j, "j", "pink", "top")],
            colors={i: "amber", j: "amber"}, note="first mismatch")
    V.array(ax, p, list(s), 0, -1.7, index=False, dim=[i], colors={k: "red" for k in range(i + 1, j + 1)},
            note=f"delete s[i] (the guess): palindrome? {left_ok}")
    V.array(ax, p, list(s), 0, -3.1, index=False, dim=[j], colors={k: "green" for k in range(i, j)},
            note=f"delete s[j]: palindrome? {right_ok}")
V.show(draw)
```

The shrunk counterexample for the guess-the-side bug. At the first mismatch both neighbours match, so the guess deletes the left character; only deleting the right one works.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time** $O(n)$: one scan to the first mismatch, then at most two palindrome checks of the rest. **Space** $O(1)$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $|s| = 1$ and strings that are already palindromes: `true` with no deletion.
- `"bba"` / `"abb"`: only one side works.
- Both neighbours match at the mismatch (the guess-the-side bug): the stress test over `"ab"` finds such strings at once, and the shrinker reduces them to a few characters.
- Do not build substrings in the loop (`s[i+1:j+1] == reversed`): it is still $O(n)$ here, but in a variant with $k$ deletions copying strings makes it much slower.
:::
